```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A prognostic risk model is a list of genes with Cox coefficients, fitted in one cohort and called validated in
another when patients with a high score fare worse. `check_models()` asks of each such validation how often a model
of the same structure, built from genes unrelated to it, passes the same test in the same cohort.

## A simulated example

A training cohort and two validation cohorts share a small co-expressed program (genes 1-10) that shortens survival,
and a large one (genes 101-250) that does not. One model takes six genes of the first program, one five of the
second, one four noise genes.

```{r simulate}
library(decoyfdr)
set.seed(1)
toy <- dfdr_toy_survival()
toy$train
toy$models$program
```

Each model of three or more genes gets 32 co-expressed and 8 random-gene decoys, matched in the training and
validation cohorts. A decoy carries its model's coefficients in a random order and takes the direction of its own
association with survival in the training cohort. Model and decoys are then tested in every validation cohort:
score split at its median, log-rank P < 0.05, high group worse.

```{r check}
chk <- check_models(toy$models, train = toy$train, validate = toy$validate, seed = 1)
chk
```

The model on the survival program validates in both cohorts and beats nearly all of its co-expressed decoys (`rho`).
Its decoys come mostly from the other program, which carries no survival information, so most of them do not
validate.

## Reading the result

`chk$units` holds one row per model and validation cohort:

```{r units}
chk$units[, c("cohort", "model", "validated", "cdir", "p", "d_coex", "d_rand", "rho")]
```

- `validated`: the rule above.
- `d_coex`: how often a model with this structure, built from unrelated genes, validates in this cohort. Summed over
  a set of models and divided by the number validated, it estimates how many validations are false:

```{r fdr}
validation_fdr(chk, B = 500)
```

- `rho`: the share of co-expressed decoys the model beats on the directed C-index. It ranks a model among models of
  its structure; it is not a test of whether the model is true. In the accompanying paper, among published models
  that validated in one cohort, those with rho of at least 0.95 there replicated in another independent cohort in
  30.5% of pairs, and the others in 21.9%.

## Cohorts differ

How often a model validates also depends on the cohort. In the paper, the usual pipeline (univariate Cox screen,
then LASSO Cox) run in TCGA on pools of genes outside every published theme and model produced null models that
validated in 0% to 85% of tries, depending on the validation cohort. `cohort_fvr()` returns that table:

```{r cohorts}
f <- cohort_fvr()
f[order(-f$fvr), c("type", "cohort", "endpoint", "patients", "events", "null_models", "fvr")][1:8, ]
cohort_fvr("GSE39582")[, c("cohort", "null_validated", "null_models", "fvr", "model_rate_not_naming")]
```

## Real data

Build one `dfdr_cohort()` per cohort from an expression matrix (genes in rows, the same gene symbols in every
cohort) and a data frame of `time` and `event`, give the models as coefficient vectors named by gene, and pass the
gene set the models were selected from to `exclude` so that the decoys come from outside it. With `cores > 1` the
result is unchanged.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
